messages:
Mae S: FYI the canary in ap-southeast-1 is showing WS liveness jitters after the routing rollout. UI shows spinner for ~6-12s mid-stream, then content resumes. No reconnect.
Ibrahim O: can you drop a raw snippet? want to see if probe frames are missing or chunks are batched.
Mae S: sanitized snippet:
```
GET /v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-x
: 200 OK
data: {"delta": "hi"}
... <7.5s silence> ...
data: {"delta": "there"}
```
Grace L: 7.5s looks suspiciously like our liveness probe TTL (7500ms). We added probe-jitter suppression to reduce noise during route handoffs. Possible suppression interacting with sticky-leases.
Ibrahim O: If probes get suppressed while a worker is being handed off, client sees no bytes -> spinner. Console counts still show the socket as OPEN because TCP isn't closed. That explains the mismatch customers are reporting.
Mae S: UX request: can we show "last payload time" for each live session in the console? Right now the table only lists open/closed + attach time. PMs keep asking why sessions appear healthy when customers see stalling.
Grace L: Yes. Also propose a small sampled trace store (0.05% of sessions) that captures byte arrival timestamps so we can surface example traces in the tile.
Ibrahim O: infra follow-up: add an edge-emitted app_heartbeat event whenever we flush a data payload to the client. Control plane can consume that and update session.last_activity.
Mae S: +1. That would let console show last_activity independent of TCP. Could add a "stalled" badge if last_activity > 5s.
Grace L: Short term mitigation: revert probe-jitter suppression on the canary region and ramp back with the heartbeat signal enabled. Also add an alert: silent_pause_rate(region) > 0.3% for 10m.
telemetry-bot: Query: silent_pause_rate(region=ap-southeast-1, last_1h) -> 0.45% ; fast_reconnect_rate -> 0.02%
Ibrahim O: So reconnect low but silent pause non-trivial. Confirms probe suppression theory rather than client churn.
Mae S: Billing question: do we risk double-charging during these stalls? Billing triggers on token/emit events, not socket lifetime. But client SDK retries can cause duplicate jobs. Need a guard.
Grace L: We should add server header x-graceful-restart: 1 during handoff windows. Then ship a tiny SDK debounce (client ignore reconnects <300ms if header present) in JS + Python. Devex can coordinate.
Ibrahim O: Action items: 1) infra: emit app_heartbeat on payload flush + sample raw byte timings for 0.05% sessions (edge label). 2) console: add last_activity column and a stalled badge (threshold configurable). 3) devex: SDK debounce + x-graceful-restart header. 4) rollback probe-jitter suppression on canary ap-southeast-1 until heartbeat is live.
rollout-bot: Rollback job queued by Mae S: revert/probe-jitter-suppression -> canary ap-southeast-1. Smoke tests: queued.
telemetry-bot: Created ticket: infra/emit-app-heartbeat-sample -> priority P2.
Mae S: I'll monitor post-rollback traces for 30m and upload a few examples to the sample pipeline. Report back here with any customer flags. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Ibrahim O: I'll take the console tile + badge work. Grace, can you coordinate SDK debounce with Devex?
Grace L: Yup, will open a small PR and tag canary. Will also add the x-graceful-restart header to the handoff flow.
Mae S: Great. If we still see stalls after this, we'll look into throttler soft-deprioritization signals — they can cause token emission gaps without 429s.
Ibrahim O: noted. We'll wire a soft_deprioritized counter into the route metrics so we can detect that next.
